title: Running through June 18th at Ars Nova in NYC! #theatre #arts #perform...
transcript: when Taylor Swift wrote about live performances shutting down in 2020, she said: “they called off the circus” “burned the disco down” “when they sent home the horses and the Rodeo clowns” “I'm still on that tightrope” “I'm still trying everything to keep you laughing at me” and it's kinda like that lyric has now been turned into an hour-long clown comedy performance And Then the Rodeo Burnt Down is a show from the rising star clown duo Xhloe and Natasha and it follows a Rodeo clown named Dale who dreams of being a cowboy and his anthropomorphized shadow who mostly dreams of Dale and as usual Xhloe and Natasha use their trademark style which blends text and fine-tuned movement work interspersed with melancholic silence to tell this resonant story about aspiration in the face of impenetrable systems. kind of a relatable theme for anyone trying to climb the “ladder” under capitalism but also maybe holding particular weight as a metaphor for the arts where the rug can really be pulled out from under you at any time. Trying not to spoil this too much, but part way through, the show takes a bit of a sharp turn that feels like something out of Samuel Beckett and I was a bit torn on it because on one hand it did create this jarring, visceral effect that I think they were going for and I appreciated the ambition of it but I think the show is just working better for me in the first half especially as the second half starts to spell out its messaging a little more explicitly and repeatedly than it may be needed to. but even with my reservations I still appreciated that the show left a lot to chew on as their work tends to do making me laugh and feel and think pretty consistently throughout. and overall I just find them such a delight to watch no matter what they're doing
reasoning: Reviewer expresses genuine appreciation and finds the duo delightful, but has notable reservations about the second half spelling out messaging too explicitly. Recommends with caveats.
